deep.reconstruction:
Context: the surrounding folios work on addition formulas for Riemann theta functions with half-integer characteristics, written in the bracket notation n+p+q+... . This page sets up the notation for characteristics. It then works out how a characteristic changes under a change of the canonical period basis, first in two elementary cases and then in general, ending with the invariance of parity.

(1) Definitions. The matrix (a_{mu,mu'}) is symmetric with negative-definite real part. The A-periods are normalised to pi*i.
- theta(v) = sum over m in Z^p of exp( sum a_{mu mu'} m_mu m_mu' + 2 sum v_mu m_mu ).
- theta[eps; eps'](v) is the same sum with m replaced by m+eps/2 and v replaced by v + eps' pi i/2.
- Expanding the quadratic form gives:
  theta[eps;eps'](v) = theta(v_1 + (1/2) sum_mu eps_mu a_{1 mu} + eps'_1 pi i/2, ...) * exp( (1/4) sum a eps eps' + sum v_mu eps_mu + (pi i/2) sum eps_mu eps'_mu ).
- This is the standard reduction of a characteristic theta to a shifted ordinary theta.
- The half-period belonging to (eps, eps') is v_mu = eps'_mu pi i/2 + sum_nu (eps_nu/2) a_{mu nu}.

(2) First elementary transformation (period scheme on the right). Riemann tabulates the periods of v_1..v_p:
- pi*i * identity on the cycles a_1..a_p;
- the matrix (a_{mu nu}) on the cycles b_1..b_p.
He introduces new variables:
- v'_nu = v_nu - (a_{nu p}/a_{pp}) v_p for nu < p;
- v'_p = v_p * pi i/a_{pp}.
This exchanges the roles of a_p and b_p:
- the b_p-period of v'_p is pi*i;
- the a_p-period of v'_p is (pi i)^2/a_pp = -pi^2/a_pp;
- the reduced entries are a_{mu nu} - a_{mu p} a_{p nu}/a_{pp}.
He computes the images of the half-period:
- v_1 - (a_{1p}/a_{pp}) v_p = eps'_1 pi i/2 + sum (eps_nu/2)(a_{1nu} - a_{1p} a_{p nu}/a_{pp}) - (eps'_p/2) pi i a_{1p}/a_{pp};
- v_p pi i/a_{pp} = -(eps'_p/2) pi^2/a_{pp} + sum (eps_nu/2) a_{nu p} pi i/a_{pp}.
The aim is to read off the new characteristic.

(3) Second elementary transformation. The new variables are v_1, ..., v_{p-1}, v_p+v_1. The new cycles are:
- a'_1 = a_1 - a_p, a'_p = a_p;
- b'_1 = b_1, b'_p = b_p + b_1.
The new period entries are:
- a'_{p1} = a_{p1} + a_{11};
- a'_{pp} = a_{pp} + 2a_{p1} + a_{11};
- a'_{1p} = a_{1p} + a_{11};
- a'_{pnu} = a_{pnu} + a_{1nu}.
Riemann rewrites the components of the half-period in the new periods. [Mine: the first such line should read v_1 = eps'_1 pi i/2 + ((eps_1-eps_p)/2) a_11 + sum eps_nu a_{1nu}/2 + (eps_p/2)(a_{1p}+a_{11}).] He writes:
- v_p+v_1 = (eps'_1+eps'_p) pi i/2 + ((eps_1-eps_p)/2)(a_{p1}+a_{11}) + sum (eps_nu/2)(a_{p nu}+a_{1nu}) + (eps_p/2)(a_{pp}+2a_{p1}+a_{11}).
He concludes that the new characteristic is ( eps_1-eps_p, eps_2, ..., eps_p ; eps'_1, eps'_2, ..., eps'_p+eps'_1 ).

(4) General transformation. A change of canonical basis is a_nu = sum_mu p^mu_nu a'_mu + q^mu_nu b'_mu and b_nu = sum r^mu_nu a'_mu + s^mu_nu b'_mu.
- It must preserve the alternating form sum (a_nu beta_nu - b_nu alpha_nu) (the intersection pairing).
- Riemann writes out the inverse substitution; the bracket coefficients are the symplectic conditions.
- The integer coefficients transform by beta'_mu = sum_nu (p^mu_nu beta_nu - r^mu_nu alpha_nu) and alpha'_mu = sum_nu (s^mu_nu alpha_nu - q^mu_nu beta_nu).

(5) Parity. Riemann expands sum_mu (sum_nu p^mu_nu eps_nu + r^mu_nu eps'_nu)(sum_nu' q^mu_nu' eps_nu' + s^mu_nu' eps'_nu').
- Modulo 2 it is sum pq eps^2 + sum eps eps' + sum rs eps'^2.
- [Mine: the cross terms reduce to sum eps eps' by the symplectic relation sum_mu (p_nu s_nu' - q_nu r_nu') = delta. The off-diagonal pq and rs terms occur twice, by the symmetry of P^T Q and R^T S, so they vanish mod 2.]
- Since eps^2 ≡ eps, the purely linear transformation changes the parity by sum_nu eps_nu sum_mu p q + eps'_nu sum_mu r s.
- So Riemann adds the diagonal corrections.

With beta = eps, alpha = -eps', beta' = eta, alpha' = -eta', the corrected law is:
- -eps'_nu ≡ -sum p^mu_nu eta'_mu + sum q^mu_nu eta_mu + sum_mu p^mu_nu q^mu_nu (mod 2);
- eps_nu ≡ -sum r^mu_nu eta'_mu + sum s^mu_nu eta_mu + sum_mu r^mu_nu s^mu_nu (mod 2).
Conclusion: sum eps_nu eps'_nu ≡ sum eta_mu eta'_mu (mod 2), i.e. the parity of a characteristic is a symplectic invariant.
errors: Line transcribed 'v_p = eps'_p/2 pi i + sum (eps_nu-eps_p)/2 a_{nu,1} + ... + eps_p/2(a_pp+a_11)' is only consistent as the v_1-component: v_1 = eps'_1 pi i/2 + (eps_1-eps_p)/2 a_11 + sum eps_nu a_{1nu}/2 + eps_p/2 (a_1p+a_11). Either the manuscript has a slip or the transcription misreads it.
In the v_p+v_1 line the 'sum' in front of (eps_1-eps_p)/2 (a_{p1}+a_{11}) is superfluous; it is a single term.

The final parity conclusion also needs sum_nu (sum_mu r s)(sum_mu p q) ≡ 0 mod 2, i.e. diag(R^T S)·diag(P^T Q) even for a symplectic matrix. The page does not show this; it is true (Igusa) but unproved here.
The vanishing mod 2 of the off-diagonal terms (nu≠nu') in sum pq eps_nu eps_nu' and sum rs eps'_nu eps'_nu' relies on the symplectic symmetry relations. This is implicit, not written.

In the scheme the new a_p-period of v_p pi i/a_pp is written pi pi/a_pp. Strictly it is (pi i)^2/a_pp = -pi^2/a_pp; the sign is absorbed by the orientation choice b'_p = -a_p. The text line has the correct minus sign.

results.what: Theta with half-integer characteristic expressed as a shifted ordinary theta times an exponential factor
results.modern_name: theta function with characteristics / quasi-periodicity shift formula

results.what: Explicit change of characteristic under the elementary basis changes (inversion a_p<->b_p; a'_1=a_1-a_p, b'_p=b_p+b_1): (eps_1-eps_p,eps_2..eps_p; eps'_1..eps'_p+eps'_1)
results.modern_name: action of Sp(2p,Z) generators on theta characteristics

results.what: Invariance of the intersection form sum(a beta - b alpha) under canonical basis change, and the induced transformation of half-period coefficients
Affine transformation of characteristics mod 2 with diagonal corrections sum_mu p q and sum_mu r s, and invariance of parity sum eps eps' mod 2
results.modern_name: theta transformation formula for characteristics, M·m = M m + (diag(CD^T), diag(AB^T)); parity invariance of even/odd characteristics
results.usually_credited_to: Hermite (1855), Thomae (1870s), Krazer–Prym; modern form Igusa (1964)

deep.surprise_reason: The material is standard theta-characteristic bookkeeping that Riemann used in his p=3 work on 28 odd characteristics and in the 1865 vanishing paper. Hermite (1855) had the transformation for p=2. A carefully worked general mod-2 law with the diagonal correction terms is a nice unpublished detail but not unexpected for Riemann.

checkable.sympy: a11,a12,a22,m1,m2,e1,e2,f1,f2,v1,v2=symbols('a11 a12 a22 m1 m2 e1 e2 f1 f2 v1 v2'); A=Matrix([[a11,a12],[a12,a22]]); m=Matrix([m1,m2]); e=Matrix([e1,e2]); f=Matrix([f1,f2]); v=Matrix([v1,v2]); lhs=((m+e/2).T*A*(m+e/2))[0]+2*((v+f*pi*I/2).T*(m+e/2))[0]; w=v+A*e/2+f*pi*I/2; rhs=(m.T*A*m)[0]+2*(w.T*m)[0]+(e.T*A*e)[0]/4+(v.T*e)[0]+pi*I/2*(e.T*f)[0]; simplify(expand(lhs-rhs))==0

transcription_corrections: The line read as 'v_p = eps'_p/2 pi i + sum (eps_nu-eps_p)/2 a_{nu,1} + sum eps_nu/2 a_{nu,p} + eps_p/2 (a_pp+a_11)' is most likely 'v_1 = eps'_1/2 pi i + (eps_1-eps_p)/2 a_{1,1} + sum eps_nu/2 a_{1,nu} + eps_p/2 (a_{1,p}+a_{1,1})'.
In the b_nu line the first bracket should be (r^mu_nu s^mu_nu' - s^mu_nu r^mu_nu'), not (r r - s r).
In the a_nu line the second bracket is (p^mu_nu' q^mu_nu - p^mu_nu q^mu_nu'), consistent with the symplectic relations.
The line 'eps_nu sum_mu r s   eps'_nu + sum_mu p q' is better read as the corrected characteristics eps_nu + sum_mu r^mu_nu s^mu_nu and eps'_nu + sum_mu p^mu_nu q^mu_nu.
